To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CERES data are consistent with the $\rho$ mass dependence of the decay width predicted by VMD.
The CERES data can be explained by the UrQMD model with a moderate mass dependent $\rho$ mesons decay width.
the CERES dilepton data can be described by UrQMD without any medium modification of rho meson properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) What is the origin of the enhancement in the invariant mass spectrum of dileptons at low invariant masses in heavy ion collisions? (ii) What are the properties of the rho meson in the nuclear environment?
the question, if dilepton spectra are useful tools to investigate the space time dynamics of the hot and dense matter created in heavy ion collisions.
the investigation of dilepton spectra in proton and heavy-ion collisions at ultrarelatistic energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both data and models need to be further improved to make more concrete statements about a possible in-medium modification of the $\rho$.
the spectral distributions of the data are consistent with the $\rho$ being a hadron and not a critical phenomenon.
the CERES data are not enough to determine the function of the $\rho$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dilepton spectra are dominantly determined by the hadronic source and that the transport properties of the medium are not the crucial point.

the dilepton spectra in the $\rho$ dominated region do not prove the formation of a thermal medium, but the possibility to study hidden strangeness in heavy ion collisions at CERN SPS is still open for $M \ge 700$ MeV.
the CERES data at 158 AGeV are only weakly sensitive to medium modifications of the $\rho$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $\rho$ decay width in the transport model is the only free parameter that is needed to explain the CERES data in the whole range of energies and systems.
the mass dependence of a hadronic form factor is important for a proper understanding of the dilepton spectra in the $\rho$-dominated region.
a strong mass dependence of the rho-nucleon cross section, as predicted by effective field theories of QCD, seems to be needed.
